title: AgentManifest v0.1 Draft
description: Canonical JSON Schema for the experimental IntentWeb AgentManifest v0.1 draft. An AgentManifest is a machine-readable website contract for AI agents that describes identity, platform, discovery, trusted knowledge, capabilities, policies, and extension points.

$schema.description: Optional JSON Schema URI or relative path used by editors and validators.

agentManifestVersion.description: Version of the AgentManifest draft used by this document.

id.description: Stable manifest identifier. Use a lowercase slug that remains stable across deployments.

templateKind.description: Template or platform family represented by this manifest, such as default, cms-wordpress, ecommerce-shopify, or framework-nextjs.

knowledge.description: Trusted public knowledge sources that agents may use when answering or planning.

capabilities.description: Business or site capabilities that agents may reason about or invoke through declared protocols.

extensionPoints.description: Optional related files, documents, catalogs, schemas, OpenAPI descriptions, MCP descriptions, policy documents, validation reports, or implementation notes.

identity.description: Public identity of the website, organization, store, service, or application represented by the manifest.

name.description: Public name of the website, organization, store, or application.

domain.description: Primary domain represented by this manifest.

owner.description: Legal or operational owner responsible for the website.

contact.description: Public contact email address or URL for manifest-related questions.

jurisdiction.description: Legal jurisdiction or operating region, if relevant.

platform.description: Implementation context for the website and the way it exposes the agent layer.

type.description: Platform category, such as generic-website, cms, frontend-framework, hosted-ecommerce, or server-rendered-website.

stack.description: Technologies, products, frameworks, or runtime components used by the website.

integrationMode.description: How the site exposes the agent layer: static files, bridge endpoints, runtime services, or an allowed combination.

servingNotes.description: Platform-specific deployment notes, routing constraints, or serving requirements for the manifest and related files.

discovery.description: Locations and related resources that help agents discover and interpret the manifest.

recommendedLocations.description: Preferred paths or URLs where agents should look for this manifest.

llmContext.description: Optional LLM-readable context files such as /llms.txt or /llms-full.txt.

openapi.description: Optional path or URL for an OpenAPI description that binds capabilities to HTTP operations.

mcp.description: Optional path or URL for MCP server metadata or connection information.

knowledgeSource.description: A trusted knowledge source exposed by the website for agent use.

type.description: Knowledge source type, such as summary, catalog, product-catalog, route-catalog, content-catalog, fulfillment-policy, or policy.

source.description: Path or URL for the knowledge source.

refresh.description: Refresh trigger or cadence, such as on deploy, on publish, daily, or on policy change.

capability.description: A capability that expresses what an agent may understand, prepare, or invoke on behalf of a user.

intent.description: Machine-readable business intent represented by this capability.

risk.description: Risk level for agent reasoning, consent behavior, audit, and policy enforcement.

stateChange.description: Whether this capability creates, changes, commits, deletes, or otherwise mutates business state.

requiresConsent.description: Whether explicit user consent is required before this capability is executed.

requiresAuthentication.description: Whether authenticated user context is required before this capability can be executed.

protocols.description: Supported execution or discovery protocols, such as static, openapi, mcp, controller, route-handler, hosted-checkout, or agent-action-gateway.

audit.description: Audit fields expected for this capability.

policies.description: Human-readable policy requirements that agents and protocol implementations must respect.

consent.description: Consent rule that agents should apply before execution.

dataMinimization.description: Rule describing which data may be exposed or collected.

pathOrUrl.description: Absolute site path, relative file path, or URI.
